source: Confucius said: There are seventy-seven disciples who have studied with me and become proficient in the six arts. They are all people with extraordinary talents. Outstanding in virtue: Yan Yuan, Min Ziqian, Ran Boniu, Zhong Gong. Those who are good at handling political affairs: Ran You, Ji Lu. In terms of language: Zaiwo, Zigong. Articles on erudition: Ziyou, Zixia. Master Zhuan Sun was extreme, Zeng Shen was slow, Gao Chai was stupid, Zhong You was rude, and Yan Hui was often poor and had nothing. Duanmuci did not accept the mercy of fate and went into business, but his predictions on the market were often accurate. The people whom Confucius respected: in the Zhou Dynasty, it was Laozi; in the Wei Kingdom, it was Zang Boyu; in the Qi Kingdom, it was Yan Zhongping; in the Chu Kingdom, it was Laolaizi; in the Zheng Kingdom, it was Zichan; in the Lu Kingdom, it was Meng Gongchuo. He also often praised Zang Wenzhong, Liu Xiahui, Tongtan Bohua, and Jieshan Ziran. Confucius was born later than them and was not of the same era. Yan Hui was from the state of Lu, his courtesy name was Ziyuan. Thirty years younger than Confucius. Yan Yuan asked what benevolence was, and Confucius said: Restrain yourself and make your words and deeds conform to etiquette, and people in the world will praise you as a virtuous person. Confucius said: Yan Hui! What a virtuous person! He ate a small bamboo basket of rice, drank a ladle of water, and lived in a simple alley. Most people couldn't bear this kind of hardship, but Yan Hui didn't change his joy. When he was listening to my teachings, Yan Hui seemed like a stupid person. After class, I examined his private conversations and showed that he was able to express himself deliberately. Yan Hui was really not stupid. When you are employed, you will save the world; when you are not employed, you will hide your secrets. Only you and I have such an attitude towards life! Yan Hui was only twenty-nine years old, his hair turned completely white, and he died prematurely. Confucius cried very sadly and said: Since I had Yan Hui, the students have become closer and closer to me. Duke Ai of Lu asked: Who among the students is the best at learning? Confucius replied: There is a man named Yan Hui who had better learn from others and never transfer his anger to others and never make the same mistake again. Unfortunately, life was short, and after death, there are no such people anymore. Min Sun, also known as Ziqian, was fifteen years younger than Confucius. Confucius said: Min Ziqian is too filial! He serves his parents and obeys his brothers. Others praise him without any criticism. He does not want to be a retainer of a high official, and he does not want to receive a salary from an emperor. So he said: If someone calls me again, I will definitely flee to the north of Wenshui River. Ran Geng, courtesy name Boniu. Confucius thought he was virtuous. Boniu was suffering from an incurable disease. Confucius went to greet him, shook his hand from the window, and said: This is life! Such a good person got such a disease, what a fate! Ran Yong, courtesy name Zhong Gong. Zhong Gong asked how to handle political affairs. Confucius said: When going out to do things, be as courteous and courteous as receiving distinguished guests, and use the people as piously and cautiously as hosting a grand ceremony. In this way, no one will resent you if you serve in the feudal state of a prince, and no one will resent you if you serve in the home of a high official. Confucius thought that Zhong Gong had achieved great achievements in virtue and said: Ran Yong, you can make him a high official like a senior official.
gold_target: Confucius identified seventy-seven disciples proficient in the six arts, categorizing them by virtue (Yan Yuan, Min Ziqian, Ran Boniu, Zhong Gong), political skill (Ran You, Ji Lu), eloquence (Zaiwo, Zigong), and erudition (Ziyou, Zixia). He noted individual traits: Zhuan Sun was extreme, Zeng Shen slow, Gao Chai stupid, Zhong You rude, and Yan Hui poor. Zigong, rejecting fate, became a successful merchant. Confucius respected figures like Laozi, Zang Boyu, Yan Zhongping, Laolaizi, Zichan, and Meng Gongchuo, and praised others from earlier eras.

He later praised the Zeng Shen, Ziyou, Zixia, and Duke Ai of Lu, who was defeated by his husbands, with many great talents and rewarding their actions.

source: Sure enough, the King of Wu fought a battle with the Qi people in Ailing and defeated the Qi army. He captured seven generals' soldiers and refused to return home. Sure enough, he led his troops to approach the Jin state and met the Jin people in Huangchi. Wu and Jin were competing for supremacy. The Jin people attacked Wu and defeated the Wu army. When the King of Yue heard the news of the Wu army's disastrous defeat, he crossed the river to attack the state of Wu. He did not set up camp until he was seven miles away from the capital of the state of Wu. When King Wu heard the news, he left Jin and returned to Wu, where he fought with the Yue army in the Five Lakes area. Many battles failed, and even the city gate could not be defended. So the Vietnamese army surrounded the palace and killed King Wu Fucha and his minister. Three years after the destruction of the Wu State, the Yue State dominated the east. Therefore, Zigong's trip saved the state of Lu, disrupted the state of Qi, destroyed the state of Wu, made the state of Jin strong, and enabled the state of Yue to dominate. Zigong's mission caused corresponding changes in the situation of various countries. Within ten years, the situations of Qi, Lu, Wu, Jin, and Yue each changed. Zigong was good at hoarding rare things, buying at low prices and selling at high prices, and changing hands to make profits according to the supply and demand situation. He likes to promote the strengths of others and does not hide the faults of others. He once served as the prime minister of Lu and Wei, and his family fortune accumulated thousands of gold. He eventually died in Qi. Yan Yan was from the state of Wu and his courtesy name was Ziyou. Forty-five years younger than Confucius. After Ziyou received his profession, he served as the governor of Wucheng. Confucius passed by Wucheng and heard the sound of playing the harp and singing. Confucius smiled slightly and said: Why use a knife to kill a chicken? Ziyou: Once upon a time, I heard my husband say: Talented people who learn rituals and music will cultivate their benevolence and love the people; ordinary people who learn rituals and music will abide by laws and regulations and be easy to control. Confucius said to the accompanying students: Everyone, what Yan Yan said is correct. What I just said was just a joke. Confucius believed that Ziyou was familiar with articles and erudite. Bu Shang, courtesy name Zixia. Forty-four years younger than Confucius. Zixia asked: "The beautiful smile is charming and moving, the bright eyes are flowing and shining, and the pure white hair of the Buddha is dyed with brilliant literary colors. What do these three sentences mean?" Confucius replied: Painting must first have a pure white background, and then decorate the picture with color. Zixia said: Did the emergence of ritual and music come after benevolence and righteousness? Confucius said: Fortune teller, now I can discuss the Book of Songs with you. Zigong asked: Which one is stronger, master Zhuan Sun or the diviner? Confucius said: Master, it's a little too much, Shang, it's a little behind. Zigong said: Is Master Zhuan Sun any better? Confucius said: Excess and failure to catch up are equally imperfect. Confucius said to Zixia: You must aspire to be a talented and virtuous scholar, not a shallow and dishonest scholar. After the death of Confucius, Zixia settled in Hexi to teach students and became the teacher of Wei Wenhou. Zixia's son died, and he cried his eyes out. Master Zhuan Sun was a native of Chen State, his courtesy name was Zizhang. Forty-eight years younger than Confucius.

source: The king of Nanyue, Wei Tuo, was from Zhending and his surname was Zhao. The Qin State annexed the six countries, captured and pacified Yang Yue, established Guilin, Nanhai and Xiangjun, and resettled the people who had committed crimes and migrated to these places, and lived together with the Yue people for thirteen years. Wei Tuo was appointed as the magistrate of Longchuan County in Nanhai County during the Qin Dynasty. During the second year of Qin Dynasty, Ren Xiao, the captain of Nanhai County, fell ill and was about to die. He summoned Zhao Tuo, the commander of Longchuan, and said to him: I heard that Chen Sheng and others had launched a rebellion, and that the Qin Dynasty was pursuing cruel and unjust policies, and the people of the world were resentful of this. Xiang Yu, Liu Bang, Chen Sheng, Wu Guang, etc. all gathered people in their respective states and counties at the same time, formed armies, and fought for the world like tigers. The Central Plains region was in turmoil, and it was unknown when peace would be restored. Heroes betrayed the Qin Dynasty and opposed each other. Nanhai County is remote and remote, and I am afraid that the bandit army will invade the land. When I attack here, I want to mobilize the army to cut off the newly built road to the Central Plains. I have taken precautions in advance and wait for the changes in the princes. It happens that I am seriously ill. Let’s talk about Panyu. There are dangerous mountains behind us to rely on, and there is the sea as a barrier to the south. It is thousands of miles away from east to west. We have some Central Plains people to assist us. We can also be the lord of a state and establish a country. There is no one among the governors of Nanhai County who is worthy of me to study these things with him, so I have summoned you to tell you these things. Ren Xiao immediately issued an appointment document to Zhao Tuo, asking him to act on behalf of Nanhai County. After Ren Xiao died, Zhao Tuo sent a message to Hengpu, Yangshan, and Huangxiguan, saying: The bandit army is coming, so we must quickly cut off the road, gather the army, and defend ourselves. Zhao Tuo took this opportunity to gradually use the law to kill the officials installed by the Qin Dynasty, and use his cronies as acting governors. source: Sima Ranju is a descendant of Tian Wan. During the period of Qi Jinggong, the Jin State sent troops to attack Qi State's Dong'a and Zhencheng, and the Yan State invaded Qi State's territory on the south bank of the Yellow River. Qi's army was defeated. Qi Jinggong was very worried about this. So Yan Ying recommended Tian Rangju to Qi Jinggong, saying: Although Rangju is the bastard of the Tian family, his literary talent can make everyone join him; his military strategy can make the enemy fear him. I hope the king can give him a try. So Qi Jinggong summoned Rangju and discussed military and state affairs with him. After discussing with him, Qi Jinggong was very happy and immediately appointed him as a general and ordered him to lead troops to resist the armies of Yan and Jin. Rangju said: "I am of a humble status. The king promoted me from the common people and placed me above the officials. The soldiers will not obey and the people will not trust me. If a person has little qualifications, authority cannot be established. I hope the king can send a minister who is favored by the king and respected by the people to supervise the army. That will be enough." So Qi Jinggong agreed to his request and sent Zhuang Jia to supervise the army. After Rang Ju bid farewell to Jinggong, she made an agreement with Zhuang Jia: "We will meet at the camp gate at noon tomorrow." The next day, Rang Ju rushed to the military gate first and set up a wooden watch and a clepsydra to wait for Zhuang Jia. However, Zhuang Jia has always been arrogant and dignified. He thinks that he is leading his own army and he is the supervisor of the army, so he is not particularly anxious. His relatives and friends bid farewell to him and invited him to drink wine. It was already noon, but Zhuang Jia had not yet arrived. Rangju knocked down the wooden watch, broke the clepsydra, entered the military camp, inspected the camp, organized the army, and issued various rules and orders. By the time he finished his deployment, it was already dusk when Zhuang Jia arrived. Rangju said: Why are you late even if you agree on the time? Zhuang Jia apologized and explained: My friends and relatives sent me off, so I was delayed. Rangju said: As a general, you should forget about your family from the moment you receive an order. When you come to the army and issue the prescribed orders, you should forget about personal friendships. When you beat the drum and march, you should forget about your own life when the battle is urgent. Now that the enemy's invasion has penetrated deep into the country, there is unrest in the country, the soldiers have been exposed on the frontline battlefield, and there is no place to hide, the monarch has trouble sleeping and eating sweetly, and the lives of the people in the country are hanging on you, so why talk about farewell! So he called the military judge and asked: According to military law, what is said about people who are late for the agreed time? The answer was: He should be beheaded. Zhuang Jia was very frightened and sent Pegasus to report to Qi Jinggong and ask him to rescue him. Not long after the messenger left, but before he could return, Zhuang Jia was beheaded and paraded in front of the three armies. The entire army was shocked and frightened. After a long time, the envoy sent by Qi Jinggong came to pardon Zhuang Jia with the festival talisman. The carriages and horses galloped straight into the military camp. Rangju said: "Generals are in the army, and they do not have to accept some of the king's orders." He also asked the military judge: "What is the military law stipulating that driving a chariot and horse galloping in the military camp?" The military judge said: He should be beheaded.

source: Tai Shigong said: When I read "Mencius", whenever I read that King Hui of Liang asked how to make profits for our country, I couldn't help but put down the book and sigh. Said: Alas, seeking profit is really the beginning of all troubles! Confucius rarely talked about the issue of profit. The reason was that he wanted to fundamentally prevent this source of trouble. So he said that acting based on personal interests will lead to a lot of resentment. From the emperor down to the common people, the disadvantages of being greedy for profit exist. What's the difference? Meng Ke was from the state of Zou. He once studied with Zisi's disciples. After he became proficient in his studies, he went to lobby King Xuan of Qi, but King Xuan of Qi did not appoint him. So when he arrived in Wei State, King Hui of Liang not only did not listen to his ideas, but also believed that his ideas were unrealistic and far from reality. At that time, all the vassal states were implementing reforms. Qin appointed Shang Yang, which made the country rich and powerful; Chu and Wei also appointed Wu Qi, who defeated some countries and weakened powerful enemies; King Wei and Xuan of Qi appointed Sun Bin and Tian Ji, etc., so that the country was strong, and all the vassal states came east to pay homage to Qi. When the vassal states were working on the offensive strategy of "joining vertical and horizontal lines" and regarded those who were good at attacking as virtuous, Mencius praised the virtues of Tang Yao, Yu Shun, and the Xia, Shang and Zhou dynasties. Therefore, it did not meet the needs of the countries he traveled around. So he returned to his hometown and worked with Wan Zhang and others to sort out the Classics and Shujing, elucidate Confucius' thoughts and doctrines, and write a book called "Mencius", a total of seven chapters. After him, scholars Zou Zi and others appeared. There are three Zouzi in the state of Qi. The earliest one was named Zou Ji. He used his piano playing skills to seek an audience with King Qi Wei. He then participated in state affairs, was named Chenghou, accepted the seal of the prime minister, and became prime minister. He lived in an era earlier than Mencius. The second one is Zou Yan, who lived after Mencius. Zou Yan witnessed that the princes who held the power of a country became more and more dissolute and extravagant, and could not advocate virtue and governance. They did not clean themselves up first and then extend it to the people as required in the "Book of Songs". So he deeply observed the ebb and flow of yin and yang of all things, and recorded the strange and mysterious changes, such as "The End and the Beginning" and "The Great Sage", totaling more than 100,000 words. His words are grand, vast, absurd and unreasonable. We must start by verifying small things, and then generalize to big things, and even reach infinity. His theory starts from the present day and then goes forward to the Yellow Emperor's era, which is discussed by scholars. Then, it generally follows the rise and fall of the generations, recording the bad and bad systems of different generations, and then pushes forward from the Yellow Emperor's era to far, far away, until the heaven and earth have not yet been formed. It is really profound and mysterious and cannot be investigated, but it is necessary to trace its origin. He first listed China's famous mountains and rivers, deep valleys, animals, water and soil vegetation, and precious species, and then promoted it to overseas countries where people could not even see it. He stated that since the beginning of the world, the five virtues of metal, wood, water, fire, and earth have been mutually reinforcing and restraining each other, and the replacement of emperors in the past dynasties has coincided with them. This is how auspiciousness from heaven corresponds to human affairs. He believes that China as mentioned by Confucianism is only one eighty-one percent of the world. It is called Chixian Shenzhou in China. There are nine states within Chixian Shenzhou, which are the nine states arranged by Xia Yu in order, but they cannot be counted as the full number of states. Outside of China, there are nine other places like Chixian Shenzhou. This is the so-called Kyushu. There are small seas surrounding this place. People and animals cannot communicate with other states. It is like an independent area. This is one state.

source: Han Feizi said: Confucian scholars quoted ancient texts to disturb the rule of law, while chivalrous men violated laws by using force. Han Fei ridiculed both types of people, but Confucian scholars were mostly praised by the world. As for using power to obtain the position of prime minister, minister, and official, assisting the contemporary emperor, and his achievements are recorded in history books, there is nothing to say about this. As for Ji Ci and Yuan Xian, they were ordinary people who studied hard, cherished the unique virtues of gentlemen, adhered to morality, and did not go along with the contemporary secular world. Contemporary people also laughed at them. Therefore, Ji Ci and Yuan Xian lived in empty thatched houses all their lives, wearing coarse clothes and not even having enough to eat. They have been dead for more than four hundred years, but their disciples from generation to generation miss them tirelessly. Although the current rangers' actions do not conform to the standards of morality and law, they must keep their word and be resolute in their actions. They must fulfill what they have promised to show their honesty and are willing to sacrifice their lives to save others in danger. He has gone through the test of life and death, but he does not boast of his abilities and is ashamed to show off his merits. This is probably something worthy of praise! Besides, critical things happen to people from time to time. Tai Shigong said: In the past, Yu Shun encountered dangers when digging wells and building houses, Yi Yin once carried Ding Chu as a cook, Fu Yue once hid in Fu Yan and did hard labor, Lu Shang once suffered hardship in Jijin, Guan Zhong once wore shackles and handcuffs, Baili Xi once fed cattle as a slave, Confucius once was besieged in Kuangdi, and suffered starvation in Chen and Kui. These people are all virtuous and benevolent people praised by Confucian scholars, but they have encountered such disasters, let alone ordinary people with moderate talents who have encountered troubled times? How can we finish talking about the disasters they encountered? Secular people have this saying: Why bother distinguishing between benevolence and righteousness? Those who have benefited are virtuous. Therefore, Boyi thought it was shameful to eat Zhou millet and starved to death in Shouyang Mountain; but King Wen and King Wu did not harm the reputation of the kings. Pirates Zhi and Zhuang Qi were cruel and brutal, but their followers praised them for their boundless morality. It can be seen from this that those who steal clothes and belt hooks will be beheaded, while those who steal state power are made marquises. People who are made marquises have benevolence and righteousness. These words are not false or untrue. Nowadays, those who stick to one-sided views, some clinging to narrow principles, and have been isolated from the world for a long time, how can they compare with those who adapt to the world with low views and follow the ups and downs of the world to gain glory and fame? As for ordinary people, they value the virtue of taking and giving in accordance with morality and fulfilling their promises. They follow morality thousands of miles away and die for morality regardless of worldly criticism. This is also their strength and cannot be done casually. Therefore, when scholars are in poverty and embarrassment, they can devote themselves to learning and face their fate. Isn't this what people call the wise and heroic people? If we compare the power, talent, and contribution of folk knight-errants to Ji Ji and Yuan Xian, they cannot be the same. In short, from the perspective of the appearance of things and the fact that one must keep one's word, how can the knight's just behavior be missing? I have never heard of civilian chivalrous people in ancient times.

source: Since the Qin Dynasty, the deeds of civilian knights have been buried and cannot be seen. I am very sorry. According to what I heard, since the founding of the Han Dynasty, there have been people such as Zhu Jia, Tian Zhong, Wang Gong, Ju Meng, and Guo Xie. Although they often violated the laws and prohibitions of the dynasty, their personal behavior was moral, honest and modest, and they were commendable. Their reputation was not falsely established, and scholars did not echo them without basis. As for those powerful people who form gangs, collude with each other, rely on their wealth to enslave the poor, use their power and violence to bully the lonely and weak, indulge their desires and satisfy themselves for their own pleasure, this is also considered shameful by the knight-errants. I feel sad that secular people cannot understand the true meaning of this, but mistakenly regard the Zhu family, Guo Xie and others as the same kind as the violent and powerful people and ridicule them together. The Zhu family of Lu State and Gaozu were of the same era. The people of Lu were educated with Confucianism, but the Zhu family was famous for being a knight. He has hid and rescued hundreds of heroes, and countless ordinary people he has saved. But he never boasted of his talents or was complacent about his kindness. Those to whom he had given favors were afraid of seeing them again. He helped others in need, starting with the poor and lowly. There was no money left in his family, his clothes were torn and incomplete, he didn't have more than two kinds of meat dishes for each meal, and his ride was just an ox-drawn cart. He was more interested in rescuing others in distress than doing anything private for himself. He once secretly saved General Ji Bu from the misfortune of being killed. However, after General Ji Bu became honored, he refused to see him again for the rest of his life. From Hangu Pass to the east, people craned their necks hoping to make friends with him. Tian Zhong of Chu was famous for being a knight. He liked swordsmanship and served the Zhu family like his father. He thought that his conduct could not keep up with the Zhu family. After Tian Zhong's death, a drama Meng appeared in Luoyang. The people of Luoyang made a living by doing business, and Ju Meng became famous among the princes because of his chivalry. When the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu rebelled, Zhou Yafu, the marquis of Tiao, was a Taiwei. He rushed to Luoyang in a post car, found Ju Meng, and said happily: The seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu launched a rebellion without asking Ju Meng for help. I know they have done nothing. The world is in turmoil, and the Taiwei getting him is like getting an equal country. Ju Meng's behavior is roughly similar to that of the Zhu family, but he likes to play chess. Most of what he does is a teenager's game. But when Ju Meng's mother passed away, there were probably thousands of cars coming from far away to mourn her. When Ju Meng died, his family didn't even have ten gold coins. At this time, Wang Meng from Fuli was also famous among the Yangtze River and Huaihe River for his chivalry. At this time, Zhou Yong of Chendi, a family named Gui in Jinan, was also famous as a hero. After Emperor Jing of the Han Dynasty heard about it, he sent envoys to kill all such people. After that, people named Bai from Daijun, Han Wupi from Liangdi, Brother Xue from Yangdi, and Han Ru from Shaanxi appeared one after another. Guo Xie was a native of Zhi County, and his courtesy name was Weng Bo. He is the grandson of Xu Ning, who is good at meeting people. Guo Xie's father was killed during the reign of Emperor Wen of Han Dynasty because he was a knight. Guo Xie was a short man, smart and strong, and he did not drink. When he was a child, he was cruel and cruel, and when he was angry and unhappy, he killed many people with his own hands. He did not hesitate to sacrifice his life to avenge his friends, hid desperadoes to commit illegal robberies, minted coins privately when he stopped, and dug graves. His illegal activities were countless. But they can be blessed by God, often escape from distress and crisis, or encounter amnesty. When Guo Xie got older, he changed his behavior, took care of himself, repaid those who hated him with kindness, gave more to others, and rarely resented others. But his own preference for Xingxia became stronger and stronger. He has saved other people's lives, but does not boast of his merits, but his heart is still cruel and vicious, and his sudden anger and violence over trivial matters are still the same as before. The young man at that time admired his behavior and often avenged him, but did not let him know. The son of Guo Xie's sister relied on Guo Xie's power to drink with others and asked them to toast. If the person's alcohol capacity is small and he can't drink anymore, he will force-fed the person. The man got angry, drew his sword, stabbed Guo Xie's sister's son to death, and then ran away.

Zhu Jia, a knight from Lu, hid and rescued hundreds without boasting, living frugally. Tian Zhong served Zhu Jia like a father. Ju Meng, from Luoyang, was sought after by Zhou Yafu during the Wu-Chu rebellion, and his mother's funeral drew thousands. The text concludes by noting that later knights were often arrogant, except for a few like Fan Zhongzi, and laments that Guo Xie's reputation outshone his unremarkable appearance and speech.

source: Tian Dan is the distant descendant of the Tian family in Qi State. During the reign of King Qi Min, Tian Dan served as a minor official in charge of the municipal administration in Linyi City, the capital, and was not reused by the King of Qi. Later, Yan State sent general Le Yi to attack Qi State, and King Qi Min was forced to flee from the capital, and soon retreated to Jucheng. When the Yan army marched in to conquer Qi, Tian Dan also left the capital and fled to Anping. He asked his people to saw off all the protruding parts of the axles at both ends and wrap them in iron sheets. Soon, the Yan army besieged Anping again, and the city was breached. The Qi people scrambled to escape. Many people were captured by the Yan army because their axles were broken. Only Tian Dan and his clansmen were able to escape because they wrapped the axle with iron hoops and retreated eastward to Jimo. At this time, the Yan army had surrendered all the cities of Qi, and only two cities, Ju and Jimo, had not yet been conquered. When the Yan army heard that King Qi Min was in Jucheng, they gathered their troops and attacked Jucheng with all their strength. Minister Nao Chi killed King Qi Min in Jucheng and defended the city against the Yan army. The Yan army did not break the city for several years. As a last resort, General Yan could only lead his troops eastward and besiege Jimo. The officials guarding the city of Jimo went out to fight with the Yan army, but were defeated and killed. The soldiers and civilians in Jimo City elected Tian Dan as their leader, saying: In the battle of Anping, Tian Dan and his fellow tribesmen were able to escape safely because they wrapped the axles with iron hoops, which shows that he knows the art of war. Therefore, everyone supported Tian Dan as general, defended Jimo, and resisted the Yan army. Not long after, King Yan Zhao died and King Yan Hui came to the throne. There was a rift between him and Le Yi. After Tian Dan heard the news, he sent people to Yan State to implement countermeasures and threatened: King Qi Min has been killed, and there are only two Qi State cities that have not been conquered. Le Yi did not dare to return home because he was afraid of being killed by the king. In the name of attacking Qi, he actually wanted to join forces with Qi's troops and become king of Qi. The people of Qi have not yet surrendered, so they are stalling for time and delaying the attack on Jimo in order to wait for the time to mature before claiming the throne. What the people of Qi are worried about is that they are afraid that Yan will send other generals. In that case, Mo City will definitely be destroyed. King Yan Hui thought these words were correct and sent his general Qi Jie to replace Le Yi. As a result, Le Yi fled to Zhao State, and the Yan officers and soldiers were very angry about this. Tian Dan also ordered the soldiers and civilians in the city to offer sacrifices to their ancestors in the courtyard before eating, causing many birds to fly around the city as they competed for the sacrificial food. Yan Jun outside the city felt strange when he saw it. Tian Dan threatened again: "This is a god descending from the sky to guide us in defeating the enemy and winning." And the people in the city said: There must be a man of god who will be my military advisor. A soldier said: Can I be your military advisor? After saying that, he walked away. Tian Dan stood up quickly, pulled him over, asked him to sit on the upper seat facing east, and served him with the etiquette of serving a teacher. The soldier said: I lied to you, I actually have no skills. Tian Dan said: Stop talking.
gold_target: Tian Dan, a distant descendant of the Qi royal family, initially served as a minor official in Linyi but was not favored by King Qi Min. When Yan's general Le Yi attacked Qi, Tian Dan fled to Anping, where he advised his people to reinforce their chariot axles with iron sheets. This precaution allowed him and his clan to escape when Anping fell, while others were captured due to broken axles. They retreated to Jimo, one of only two Qi cities not conquered by Yan.

source: Ranghou Wei Ran was the younger brother of the Queen Mother Xuan, the mother of King Zhao of Qin. His ancestor was from the Chu state and his surname was Mi. After the death of King Qin Wu, he had no sons, so he made his younger brother the king of the country, namely King Zhao. King Zhao's mother was originally a female official in the palace and was called Mi Bazi. When King Zhao came to the throne, Mi Bazi was revered as Queen Mother Xuan. Queen Mother Xuan was not King Wu’s biological mother. King Wu's mother was Queen Huiwen, who died before King Wu died. Empress Dowager Xuan has two younger brothers: her eldest half-brother is named Ranghou, whose surname is Wei and given name is Ran; her half-brother is named Mirong, who is Huayang Jun. King Zhao also has two younger brothers with the same mother: one is called Gaolingjun and the other is named Jingyangjun. Among many people, Wei Ran was the most virtuous. He had been in power since the time of King Hui and King Wu. After King Wu died, his younger brothers competed to inherit the throne. Only Wei Ran was capable and supported King Zhao. After King Zhao ascended the throne, he appointed Wei Ran as general to guard Xianyang. He once put down the rebellion of Ji Jun Gongzi Zhuang and some ministers, and expelled Queen Wu to the state of Wei. All the brothers of King Zhao who had evil intentions were killed. Wei Ran's prestige shocked the state of Qin for a while. At that time, King Zhao was still young, so Empress Dowager Xuan personally presided over the affairs of the court, leaving Wei Ran in charge. In the seventh year of King Zhao, Chuilizi died, and the State of Qin sent Lord Jingyang to Qi State as a hostage. Zhao Guoren Lou slowly came to Qin State to serve as prime minister, which was obviously not good for Zhao State, so Zhao State sent Qiu Lie to Qin State to lobby, requesting that Wei Ran be allowed to serve as Qin State's prime minister. Qiu Ye was about to leave, and his retainer Song Gong said to Qiu Ye: If the King of Qin does not listen to your persuasion, Lou Huan will definitely resent you. Why don't you tell Lou Huan, please plan for you, I will have some reservations in persuading the King of Qin to appoint Wei Ran as prime minister. The King of Qin must be surprised to see that the envoy from Zhao is not eager to appoint Wei Ran, and will not listen to your suggestion. You said this, if things don't work out, the King of Qin will appoint Lou Huan as his prime minister, and you will gain Lou Huan's favor; if things succeed, and the King of Qin will appoint Wei Ran as his prime minister, then Wei Ran will be grateful to you. So Qiu Ye listened to Song Gong's advice. As expected, the State of Qin deposed Lou Huan and made Wei Ran the prime minister. King Zhao of Qin wanted to kill Lu Li, so Lu Li fled to Qi. In the fourteenth year of King Zhao, Wei Ranju appointed Bai Qi as general and sent him to lead the army to attack Han and Wei instead of Xiang Shou. He defeated them at Yique, killed 240,000 enemies, and captured Wei general Gongsun happy. The next year, he captured the two cities of Wan and Ye in Chu State. After that, Wei Ran was dismissed due to illness, and the King of Qin appointed his guest Qing Shouzhu as the prime minister. The next year, Shouzhu was dismissed and Wei Ran was appointed as prime minister. Wei Ran was granted the title of Rangdi, and later he was granted the title of Taoyi and was called Ranghou. Four years after Ranghou was granted the title, he served as the general of Qin and led troops to attack Wei. Wei was forced to surrender four hundred miles of land east of the river. Later, he occupied the Hanoi area of ​​Wei State and captured more than 60 cities, large and small.

source: Su Qin was a native of Luoyang in the Eastern Zhou Dynasty. He went east to Qi State to study under Mr. Guiguzi. After traveling for many years, he was impoverished and returned home in embarrassment. Brothers and sisters-in-law, younger brothers and sisters, wives and concubines all laughed at him privately, saying: "It is the custom of the Zhou people that people manage their industries, work hard in industry and commerce, and pursue the two-tenths of profits as their career." Now you have abandoned your profession and gone to talk, and you are in poverty, isn't that right? After hearing these words, Su Qin felt secretly ashamed and sad, so he stayed behind closed doors and read all his books. Said: Since a scholar has been taught by a teacher and immersed himself in reading, but he cannot obtain status and glory through it, no matter how much he reads, what is the use? So I found a book called "Yin Fu" and sat down at my desk to study it. After working hard for a whole year, he searched for the truth and found a way to get along with the king. He said excitedly: With these alone, I can persuade the king of today. He asked to see and lobby King Xian of Zhou. However, the ministers around King Xian always knew Su Qin's character and looked down upon him. Therefore, King Xian of Zhou did not trust him either. So he went west to the state of Qin. Duke Xiao of Qin is dead. He persuaded King Hui and said: Qin is a country surrounded by dangerous mountains. The Wei River flows like a belt, with Hangu Pass and the Yellow River in the east, Hanzhong in the west, Bashu in the south, Daima and Mayi in the north. This is really a dangerous, fertile and abundant natural treasury. With its numerous people and well-trained soldiers, the Qin State was able to annex the world, establish an empire, and rule all directions. King Hui of Qin said: It is impossible for a bird to fly in the sky before its feathers are full; the country's political and religious affairs are not on the right track, and it is impossible to annex the world. At this time, the state of Qin had just executed Shang Yang and hated the lobbyists very much, so it did not appoint Su Qin. So, he went east to the state of Zhao. Zhao Suhou appointed his younger brother Zhao Cheng as the prime minister of the country, with the title Fengyang Jun. Lord Fengyang doesn't like Su Qin. Su Qin left Zhao State again and traveled to Yan State. It took more than a year before he had the opportunity to meet Yan Wenhou. He advised Marquis Wen of Yan: The country of Yan is bounded by Korea and Liaodong to the east, Linhu and Loufan to the north, Yunzhong and Jiuyuan to the west, and Tuohe and Yishui to the south. The country stretches for more than two thousand miles, has hundreds of thousands of soldiers, 600 chariots, and 6,000 horses, and has enough food stored for several years. In the south, the land in Jieshi Mountain and Yanmen Mountain is fertile and rich in products; in the north, you can grow red dates and chestnuts to gain income. Even if the people do not farm, the income from red dates and chestnuts alone can ensure that they live a prosperous life. This is the so-called natural treasury. The people can live and work in peace and contentment, there is no war, and they will not face the danger of the army being destroyed and the generals and soldiers being killed. No one can compare with the Yan State in this regard. Does your Majesty know the reason for this? The reason why Yan State was not invaded by enemies was that Zhao State was Yan State's barrier in the south. Qin and Zhao launched five wars, Qin won twice and Zhao won three times.

Su Qin left Zhao State again and traveled to Yan State. It took more than a year before he had the opportunity to meet Yan Wenhou. He advised Marquis Wen of Yan: The country of Yan is bounded by Korea and Liaodong to the east, Linhu and Loufan to the north, Yunzhong and Jiuyuan to the west, and Tuohe and Yishui to the south. The country stretches for more than two thousand miles, has hundreds of thousands of soldiers, 600 chariots, and 6,000 horses, and has enough food stored for several years. In the south, the land in Jieshi Mountain and Yanmen Mountain is fertile and rich in products; in the north, you can grow red dates and chestnuts to gain income. Even if the people do not farm, the income from red dates and chestnuts alone can ensure that they live a prosperous life. This is the so-called natural treasury. The people can live and work in peace and contentment, there is no war, and they will not face the danger of the army being destroyed and the generals and soldiers being killed. No one can compare with the Yan State in this regard. Does your Majesty know the reason for this? The reason why Yan State was not invaded by enemies was that Zhao State was Yan State's barrier in the south. Qin and Zhao launched five wars, Qin won twice and Zhao won three times. The two countries are killing each other and destroying each other, but the king can rely on the intact power of the Yan State to control them from behind. This is the reason why the Yan State is not invaded by enemy countries. Moreover, if Qin wanted to attack Yan, it would have to travel through Yunzhong and Jiuyuan, pass through Daijun and Shanggu, and travel thousands of miles. Even if it could capture Yan's city, Qin would consider that it had no way to defend it. It is already very obvious that Qin cannot invade Yan. Now that the State of Zhao wants to attack the State of Yan, as long as it issues an order, it will not take ten days for hundreds of thousands of troops to be stationed in the Donghuan area on the border. The Zhao army will then cross the Tuo River and ford the Yishui River. It will not take more than four or five days to reach the capital of the State of Yan. Therefore, when Qin attacked Yan, it had to fight thousands of miles away; when Zhao attacked Yan, it only fought within a hundred miles. There is no more wrong strategy than not worrying about disasters within a hundred miles, but focusing on enemies thousands of miles away. Therefore, I hope that your Majesty can unite with the State of Zhao and unite all countries into one, so that there will be no trouble for the State of Yan. Marquis Yan Wen said: Of course you are right, but my country is weak, close to the powerful Zhao State in the west, and close to Qi and Zhou in the south. Qi and Zhao are both powerful countries. You must use the method of marriage and marriage to make the Yan country safe and sound. I am willing to surrender the country to you. So he funded Su Qin's carriage, horses and money to travel to Zhao. Lord Fengyang was dead, so he took the opportunity to lobby Zhao Suhou: "Every minister in the world, right down to the scholars in rough clothes, all admire you as a wise king for your benevolence and righteousness, and they all hope to listen to your teachings and give your loyal advice in front of you. It has been a long time." Even so, Lord Fengyang is jealous of talents and you ignore political affairs, so no guests or lobbyists dare to speak freely in front of you.

He proposed a united front of six states against Qin, detailing how each state would support the others if attacked. King Zhao accepted, providing resources for Su Qin to persuade other states.

source: With the wisdom of the king and the strength of Qi, no country in the world can compare with it. Now that you have to go west to serve Qin, I feel ashamed for your Majesty. Moreover, the reason why Han and Wei are very afraid of Qin is because they are bordering Qin. If both sides send troops to fight, the situation of victory or defeat will be decided in less than ten days. If Han and Wei defeated Qin, they would lose half of their troops and their borders would be unable to be defended; if they could not win the battle, then the country would be in danger. This is why Han and Wei regard fighting with Qin as so important and want to surrender to Qin so easily. Now, the situation of Qin's attack on Qi is different. Qin's back is backed by the lands of Han and Wei, and it has to pass through Wei's Yangjin stronghold and Qi's Kangfu's dangerous fortress. Chariots cannot drive side by side, and war horses cannot run parallel. As long as a hundred people guard the dangerous place, even a thousand people dare not pass. Even if the Qin army wants to go deep, it will be like wolves with doubts, often looking back, fearing that Han and Wei are plotting against it behind. So it's bluffing, intimidating and threatening. Although it is arrogant and boastful, it does not dare to risk attacking, so it is quite clear that Qin cannot harm Qi. They failed to fully understand the fact that Qin State was basically helpless against Qi State, but wanted to go west to serve Qin State. This was a strategic mistake among the ministers. Now, Qi State has not yet had the ugly reputation of surrendering to Qin State, but it has strong national strength, so I hope that the king will consider it carefully in order to decide on countermeasures. King Qi said: I am not a smart person. I live in a remote country, close to the sea, with no roads, and located in the east. I have never heard your wise teachings. Now that you have come to teach me on the mission of King Zhao, I will solemnly lead the people of the country to obey your arrangements. So Su Qin went southwest to lobby King Wei of Chu, saying: "The Kingdom of Chu is the most powerful country in the world; your Majesty, the Kingdom of Chu is the wise king in the world." Chu State has Qianzhong and Wujun in the west, Xiazhou and Haiyang in the east, Dongting and Cangwu in the south, and Jingsai and Xiyang in the north. It has a land of more than 5,000 miles and has an armed force of one million, thousands of chariots, and tens of thousands of horses. It has enough grain to last ten years. This is the capital to build hegemony. With the power of Chu and the wisdom of the king, no country in the world can match it. Now that you want to serve Qin to the west, there will be no prince in the world who will not bow to the west and submit to Qin's Zhangtai Palace. Qin's greatest worry is no greater than that of Chu. If Chu is strong, Qin will be weak; if Qin is strong, Chu will be weak. Judging from this situation, the two countries cannot coexist at the same time. Therefore, I advise your majesty to plan, it is better to join forces and have a blind date to isolate Qin. If the king does not adopt the policy of cooperation, Qin will definitely send two armies, one to attack from Wuguan, and the other to go straight to central Guizhou. Then the situation in Yanying will be shaken. I heard that we should control unrest before it occurs, and take action before disaster strikes. If you wait until disaster strikes before you worry about it, it will be too late. So I hope your Majesty can make careful plans early. If the king really listens to my advice, I can make all the countries in Shandong offer you the gifts of the four seasons, accept your wise guidance, entrust the country to you, dedicate ancestral temples for your protection, train soldiers, sharpen weapons, and obey the king's command. If the king can really adopt my immature strategy, then your harem will surely be filled with the beautiful music and beautiful women of Han, Wei, Qi, Yan, Zhao, Wei and other countries. Camels and fine horses produced in the lands of Yan and Dai will surely fill your pen. Therefore, if the alliance is successful, Chu will be able to become king. If Lian Heng succeeds, Qin will be able to proclaim himself emperor. Now you have to give up your career as king and gain the reputation of serving others. I privately think that this approach of your Majesty is not advisable. Qin is a country as ferocious as tigers and wolves, and has the ambition to annex the world. Qin is also the common enemy of all the princes in the world. Anyone who advocates Lianheng wants to divide the land of various princes and offer it to Qin. This is called supporting the enemy and worshiping the enemy.
gold_target: Su Qin then approached King Xuan of Han, highlighting Korea's military strength and warning that serving Qin would lead to endless land demands. King Han angrily refused to serve Qin. He similarly persuaded King Wei of Wei, stressing Wei's power and the folly of ceding land to Qin. King Wei agreed to follow Su Qin's plan. In Qi, he advised King Xuan that Qin could not easily attack Qi due to geographical barriers, and that serving Qin was a strategic error. King Qi consented. Finally, he lobbied King Wei of Chu, arguing that Chu and Qin could not coexist and that alliance would bring glory. King Wei, fearing Qin's ambition, entrusted his state to Su Qin.

source: Su Qin became the leader of the United Vertical Alliance and concurrently served as the Prime Minister of the Six Nations. Su Qin went north to return his order to King Zhao. On the way, he passed Luoyang. The accompanying vehicles and horses were fully loaded with luggage. There were many envoys sent by the princes to see him off, and they were as grand as the emperor. King Xian of Zhou Dynasty was frightened when he heard the news. He quickly found someone to clear the road for him and sent envoys to the suburbs to greet him. Su Qin's brothers, wife, and sister-in-law squinted and did not dare to look up at him. They all fell down on the ground and served him with great respect. Su Qin smiled and said to his sister-in-law: Why were you so arrogant to me before, but now you are so deferential to me? His sister-in-law quickly fell to the ground, bent her body, and crawled in front of him. She put her face to the ground and apologized, saying: "Because I saw that uncle, you have a high status and a lot of money." Su Qin sighed with emotion and said: I am the same person. When I am rich, my relatives will respect me, but when I am poor, they will despise me. Not to mention ordinary people! If I had two hectares of fertile farmland in the suburbs of Luoyang back then, would I still be able to wear the seals of six countries now? At that time, he distributed thousands of gold coins and gave them to relatives and friends. When Su Qin went to the State of Yan, he borrowed one hundred gold from someone for travel expenses. Now that he was rich, he borrowed one hundred gold to repay that person. And he repaid all those who had been kind to him in the past. Among his entourage, there was only one person who did not receive the reward, so he went forward to plead his case. Su Qin said: "I have not forgotten you. When you came to Yan State with me, you tried to leave me again and again by the Yishui River. At that time, I was in dire straits, so I deeply blamed you, so I put you last. Now you can also get the reward." After Su Qin agreed on the alliance of the six countries, he returned to the State of Zhao. Marquis Su of Zhao named him Lord Wu'an, so Su Qin sent the alliance to Qin. From then on, Qin State did not dare to spy on countries outside Hangu Pass for fifteen years. Later, Qin State sent envoy Xishou to deceive Qi State and Wei State, and joined forces with them to attack Zhao State, intending to destroy the alliance. Qi and Wei attacked Zhao, and the king of Zhao blamed Su Qin. Su Qin was afraid and asked to send an envoy to Yan State to take revenge on Qi State. After Su Qin left Zhao, the alliance collapsed. King Hui of Qin married his daughter to the prince of Yan as his wife. In this year, Marquis Wen of Yan died and the prince ascended the throne. This was King Yi of Yan. King Yi had just ascended the throne, and King Xuan of Qi took advantage of Yan's mourning to attack Yan and captured ten cities in a row. The King of Yi said to Su Qin: Once upon a time, Sir, when you came to the Kingdom of Yan, the late king sponsored you to meet the King of Zhao, and then we agreed on the alliance of the six kingdoms. Now the State of Qi first attacks the State of Zhao, and then the State of Yan, and is ridiculed by the world because of the Master. Can the State of Qi regain the occupied territory for the State of Yan? Su Qin felt very ashamed and said: Please let me take back the lost land for the king. When Su Qin saw the King of Qi, he bowed twice, bent down to express his congratulations to the King of Qi, and raised his head to express his condolences to the King of Qi.
gold_target: The six states united, with Su Qin as their leader and prime minister. On his return to Luoyang, his family, once scornful, now bowed in awe. He distributed wealth to relatives and repaid debts. The alliance kept Qin from invading for fifteen years. However, Qin later deceived Qi and Wei into attacking Zhao, breaking the pact. Su Qin fled to Yan, where King Yi sought his help to recover ten cities lost to Qi. Su Qin persuaded King Qi to return them by warning of Qin's enmity. Despite slander, Su Qin regained King Yan's trust, though he had an affair with the king's mother. Fearing death, he feigned offense and fled to Qi, where he served as a guest minister. He secretly plotted to weaken Qi for Yan, advising King Min to waste resources on grand projects. Eventually, rivals assassinated him. Before dying, he told King Qi to display his body publicly, promising the assassin would be caught. The ruse worked, and the assassin was executed.
generated: In the first year, Marquis Wen of Yan died, killing him as prince, and he returned to the State of Zhao. After his death, he sent a envoy to Wangu Pass for fifteen years.

source: The State of Wei believed that what he said was reasonable, so he served the State of Qin. Qin planned to attack Anyi and was worried that Qi would rescue it, so it promised the land of Song to Qi. Said: The King of Song was ignorant, so he made a wooden man that looked like me, and shot it in the face with arrows. My country was cut off from Song, and the army was too far away from Song to attack it directly. King Qi, if you can defeat the Song State and take it as your own, you will be as happy as I would be if I took it for myself. Later, the Qin State captured Anyi of the Wei State and besieged Nuji. Instead, it regarded the defeat of the Song State as Qi's crime. Qin planned to attack South Korea and was worried that the princes of the world would rescue it, so it promised Qi to the princes of the world to attack it, saying: The king of Qi made an alliance with me four times, deceived me four times, and resolutely led the army of the world to attack our country, many times. As long as Qi exists, there will be no Qin. As long as Qin exists, there will be no Qi. It must be conquered and destroyed. When the Qin State captured Yiyang and Shaoqu in South Korea and conquered Linyi and Lishi, it regarded defeating the Qi State as a sin among the vassal states in the world. Qin planned to attack Wei, so he first respected Chu and promised Nanyang to Chu. Said: I had already severed ties with South Korea. If it is beneficial to the state of Chu to destroy Junling and besiege it, then I will be as happy as if I had it. When the state of Wei abandoned the alliance and joined forces with the state of Qin, the state of Qin charged Chu with siege. Qin's army was trapped in the forest, so he respected Yan and Zhao, and promised Jiaodong to Yan and Jixi to Zhao. When Qin and Wei reconciled, they took Gongzi Yan as a hostage and used rhinoceros troops to attack Zhao one after another. Qin's army suffered heavy losses at Qiaoshi and was defeated at Yangma, so he respected Wei and granted the land of Ye and Cai to Wei. After he reconciled with Zhao, he threatened Wei and refused to divide the land as agreed. When the Qin army was in trouble, they sent the Queen Mother's brother Ranghou to make peace. When he won, even his uncle and mother were deceived. Outside Xihe, the Shangluo area and Sanchuan area are often attacked by the Qin State. This is a disaster for the Jin State! The Qin State invaded half of the land of Han, Zhao, and Wei. The disasters caused by the Qin State were so serious! However, people from Yan, Zhao and other countries who went to Qin to persuade their kings tried to persuade their own monarchs by serving Qin. This is something that worries me very much. King Yan Zhao did not go to Qin, and Su Dai was reused by King Yan again. The King of Yan sent Su Dai to contact the various countries to unite and establish a blind date. Just like when Su Qin was alive, some princes joined the alliance and some did not. People from all over the world respected the alliance advocated by Su Qin from then on. Both Su Dai and Su Li lived to a very old age, and their reputations became prominent in various vassal states. Tai Shigong said: The three brothers Su and Qin are famous all over the world for lobbying the princes. Their theories are good at maneuvering and maneuvering. However, Su Qin was killed on the charge of counter-intentional conspiracy. Everyone in the world laughed at him and tabooed the study of his teachings. However, there are many differences in the deeds of Su Qin circulated in society. All deeds similar to Su Qin in different periods are attached to Su Qin. Su Qin was born among the common people, but he was able to unite six countries and have a blind date. This shows that his intelligence is beyond ordinary people. Therefore, I will list his experiences and state them in the correct chronological order, so as not to let him only suffer a bad reputation.
gold_target: Su Qin's brothers, Su Dai and Su Li, later pursued similar careers. After Su Qin's death, Su Dai served Yan, advising King Yan on strategy against Qi. He noted Qi's exhaustion from wars and suggested using bribes to manipulate Qi into attacking Song, weakening itself. King Yan agreed. Su Li also served Qi, but faced suspicion due to Su Qin's past. The brothers eventually fled to Qi after Yan's internal chaos. Su Dai later returned to Yan, helping King Zhao plan and execute a successful attack on Qi, forcing King Min to flee. Su Dai later advised King Yan against visiting Qin, warning of Qin's violent tactics. King Yan heeded this advice. Both Su Dai and Su Li lived to old age, renowned for their diplomatic skills.
generated: In the historical reports, Su Qin and Su Li remained prominent in their reputations, and his morality was weak, and Liu Gao sought to persuade kings for maintaining alliances. Su Qin, from common people, defeated Yuiyang and Shaoqu.

article_path: 史记/七十列传/货殖列传
source: As for the situation since the Yu and Xia dynasties described in the "Poems" and "Books", the ears and eyes want to enjoy the beauty of music and female sex, the mouth wants to taste all kinds of meat and delicacies, and they live in debauchery and pleasure, and their hearts boast about the glory of power. This evil custom has been used to infect the people for a long time. Even if you use Lao Tzu's wonderful theories to persuade and enlighten them door to door, you will never be able to change them. So the best way is to let nature take its course, the second is to take advantage of the situation, the third is to educate them, the third is to correct their behavior, and the worst way is to fight with them. The west of Mount Wei is rich in wood, bamboo, mulberry, wild hemp, oxtail, and jade; the east of Mount Mount is rich in fish, salt, lacquer, silk, and beauties; the south of the Yangtze River is rich in nanmu, catalpa, ginger, osmanthus, gold, tin, lead, cinnabar, Rhinoceros, tortoise shells, beads, and ivory skins; Longmen and the area north of Jieshi Mountain are rich in horses, cattle, sheep, felt fur, animal sinews and horns; copper and iron are distributed thousands of miles around, and the mountains are everywhere, like chess pieces. This is the general situation about the distribution of products in various places. These are the things that the Chinese people like and use to wear, eat, maintain health, and prepare for death. Therefore, people rely on farmers to cultivate and obtain food, they rely on Yu people to mine in the mountains and fishermen to hunt in the water to obtain items, they rely on craftsmen to manufacture and obtain utensils, and they rely on merchants to trade and circulate goods. Does this still require the government to issue a decree, recruit people, and gather within a time limit? People rely on their own talents and do their best to satisfy their own desires. Therefore, low-priced goods can be sold at high prices, and high-priced goods can be purchased at low prices. People work hard at their own business and are happy to do their own work, just like water flowing from high to low. Day and night without end, they will come automatically without being called, and they will be produced without asking. Isn’t this proof that it follows the laws and develops naturally? "Book of Zhou" says: If farmers don't farm, there will be a shortage of food; if craftsmen don't work and produce, there will be a shortage of utensils; if merchants don't do business, the three treasures of food, use, and money will be cut off; if the Yu people don't develop mountains and rivers, there will be a shortage of resources. If resources are scarce, mountains and rivers cannot be further developed. The four fields of agriculture, industry, commerce, and agriculture are the sources of food and clothing for the people. If the source is large, the country will be rich; if the source is small, the country will be poor; if the source is large, it can make the country rich and strong, and if it is small, it can make the family rich. Rich or poor, no one can take away or give to others, but smart people always have more than enough wealth, while stupid people often have insufficient food and clothing. Therefore, when Jiang Taigong was sealed in Yingqiu, it was mostly saline-alkali land and sparsely populated. So Jiang Taigong encouraged women to devote themselves to textile and embroidery, strongly promoted craft skills, and asked people to transport fish and sea salt back to other areas. As a result, people and property from other countries flowed back to Qi State, like ropes connected to each other, in an endless stream, like the spokes of a car gathered at the hub, gathering there from all directions.
gold_target: It argues that human desires for pleasure, wealth, and power are deeply ingrained and cannot be changed by persuasion. The best governance, therefore, is to let nature take its course, followed by guiding, educating, and correcting, with conflict as the last resort.

source: Taibo Wu and his younger brother Zhong Yong were both sons of Gu Gong Danfu, King Tai of Zhou, and brothers of Ji Li, King of Zhou. Ji Li was very virtuous and had a virtuous son Chang. Like the local barbarians, they covered their bodies with tattoos and cut their hair to show that they could no longer inherit the throne, so as to avoid Ji Li. Ji Li succeeded to the throne as Wang Ji, and Chang later became King Wen. After Taibo fled to Jingman, he called himself Wu Ju. The Jingman people believed that he was very righteous, and more than a thousand households followed him and respected him as Taibo Wu. Taibo died without a son, and his younger brother Zhongyong succeeded him; he was Wu Zhongyong. Zhongyong died and his son Ji Jian succeeded to the throne. Ji Jian died and his son Shuda succeeded him. Shuda died and his son Zhou Zhang succeeded to the throne. At that time, King Wu defeated Yin Zhou and was looking for the descendants of Tai Bo and Zhong Yong, and found Zhou Zhang. Zhou Zhang was already the monarch of Wu, so King Wu officially granted him the land of Wu. He also enfeoffed Zhou Zhang's younger brother Yu Zhong to the former site of the Xia capital in the north of Zhou Dynasty. He was named Yu Zhong and ranked among the princes. Zhou Zhang died and his son Xiong Sui succeeded to the throne. Xiong Sui died, and his son Ke succeeded him. Ke Xiang died and his son Qiang Jiuyi succeeded to the throne. Qiang Jiuyi died, and his son Yu Qiaoxinwu succeeded to the throne. Yu Qiao Xinwu died, and his son Ke Lu succeeded to the throne. Ke Lu died and his son Zhou Yao succeeded him. Zhou Yao died and his son Qu Yu succeeded him. Qu Yu died and his son Yi Wu succeeded him. Yiwu died and his son Qinchu succeeded him. Qin Chu died and his son succeeded him. After his death, his son Po Gao succeeded him. Po Gao died and his son Goubei succeeded him. At this time, Duke Xian of Jin destroyed Duke Yu who was north of the Zhou Dynasty, because Duke Yu lent a road to the Jin State, allowing the Jin army to destroy the Guo State. Goubei died, and his son went to Qi to succeed him. Qu Qi died, and his son Shou Meng succeeded to the throne. After Shou Meng succeeded to the throne, the Kingdom of Wu began to become stronger, and Shou Meng called himself the king. Counting from Taibo's founding of the Kingdom of Wu to the fifth generation, King Wu defeated the Yin Dynasty and named his descendants two kingdoms: one was the Kingdom of Yu, in the Central Plains, and the other was the Kingdom of Wu, in the barbarian zone. By the twelfth generation, the Jin State destroyed the Yu State in the Central Plains. Two more generations later, the state of Wu in the barbarian region became prosperous. In total, it has been passed down to nineteen generations from Taibo to Shoumeng. In the second year of King Shoumeng of Wu, the exiled official Shen Gong Wuchen of the Chu State defected to the Jin State because he was resentful of the generals of the Chu State. Shoumeng had four sons: the eldest son was named Zhufan, the second son was named Yuji, the third son was named Yumei, and the fourth son was named Jizha. Ji Zha was a virtuous man, and Shou Meng wanted him to succeed him during his lifetime, but Ji Zha evaded and refused to agree, so he let his eldest son Zhufan succeed him, prime minister of various affairs, and take charge of state affairs on his behalf.

source: Chen Wan is Chen Ligong's son. When Wan was born, Taishi of Zhou happened to pass by the state of Chen. Chen Ligong asked him to divine divination for Chen Wan. Does this mean that he will obtain the throne of Chen and own the country? Maybe it's not in Chen country but in another country? Or it may not be fulfilled on others, but be fulfilled on his descendants. If it is in another country, it must be the country with the surname Jiang. The surname Jiang is a descendant of the Four Mountains during the reign of Emperor Yao. It is impossible for two things to be powerful at the same time. After the decline of Chen State, his branch will prosper! Li Gong is the youngest son of Chen Wengong, and his mother is a woman from Cai State. After Duke Wen died, Duke Li's brother Chen Bao came to the throne, and this was Duke Huan. Duke Huan and his younger brother Chen were not born from the same mother. When Duke Huan was ill, the people of Cai killed Duke Huan Chen Bao and Prince Chen Min on behalf of Chen Ta, and made Chen Ta the king. This is Duke Li. After Li Gong came to the throne, he married a woman from Cai State. This Cai woman committed adultery with a Cai man and returned to Cai many times. Duke Li also frequently went to Cai. Chen Lin, the youngest son of Duke Huan, resented Duke Li for killing his father and brother, so he asked the people of Cai to trick Duke Li and kill him. Chen Lin established himself as king, this is Duke Zhuang. Therefore, Chen Wan could not be established as the king, but only as the official of the state of Chen. Yu Kou and Chen Wan were close, and he was afraid that the disaster would involve him, so Chen Wan fled to Qi State. Duke Huan of Qi wanted to appoint him as minister, but he declined and said: "As a humble minister living abroad, I am fortunate enough to be exempted from all kinds of burdens. It is already a favor given to me by you. I dare not hold such a high position again." Duke Huan of Qi appointed him as Gongzheng in charge of hundreds of workers. Qi Yizhong wanted to marry his daughter to Chen Wan, so he conducted a divination for this matter. The result of the divination said: This is called the flying phoenix, with a harmonious sound. The descendants of the Gui family will grow up under the Jiang family. After the Five Dynasties, he will be prosperous and have the same status as Zhengqing. After eight generations, no one can be higher than him. He finally married his daughter to Chen Wan. When Chen Wan fled to Qi, Duke Huan of Qi had been in power for fourteen years. The kings of Zou and Lu did not accept him, so he ran to Ju again. At this time, the state of Chu sent Nao Chi to lead troops to rescue the state of Qi, so he assisted King Min of Qi. Tian Dan relied on Jimo's army and people to defeat the Yan army, went to Ju to welcome King Xiang, and returned to Linzi. All the original land of Qi State was returned to Qi State. In the nineteenth year, King Xiang died and his son Tian Jian came to the throne. Six years after King Jian of Qi came to the throne, Qin attacked Zhao, and Qi and Chu went to rescue it. The state of Qin planned to say: Qi and Chu come to the rescue of Zhao. If they are close to each other, we will retreat; if they are not close, we will attack them. Zhao State had no food and asked Qi State for grain support, but Qi State refused. Zhouzi said: It is better to agree to it so that the Qin soldiers will retreat. If you don't agree to it, the Qin soldiers will not retreat. In this way, Qin's strategy will succeed, but Qi and Chu's strategies will fail. Moreover, the State of Zhao is a barrier to Qi and Chu, just like there are lips outside the teeth. Without the lips, the teeth will get cold. Today the State of Zhao is destroyed, and tomorrow the disaster will come to the States of Qi and Chu. Moreover, rescuing Zhao should be like holding a leaky urn to pour out a burnt pot. Saving Zhao is a noble act of justice; causing Qin soldiers to retreat will show their prestige. It is a mistake to act righteously to save a dying country and to use force to defeat the powerful Qin army. Those who do not try their best to do this but focus on sparing food and making suggestions for the country are wrong. The king of Qi did not listen to the advice. The Qin army defeated more than forty troops of Zhao State in Changping, and then surrounded Handan. In the 16th year of the founding of King Qi, the Qin State destroyed the Zhou Dynasty. The king and queen of Qi died. In the twenty-third year of the Qin Dynasty, the State of Qin established Dongjun. In the twenty-eighth year, the King of Qi went to Qin to pay homage, and the King of Qin hosted a banquet in Xianyang. In thirty-five years, Qin destroyed South Korea. In the thirty-seventh year, Qin State destroyed Zhao State. In the thirty-eighth year, the State of Yan sent Jing Ke to assassinate the King of Qin. The King of Qin found out and killed Jing Ke. The next year, the Qin army captured the capital of Yan, and the king of Yan fled to Liaodong. In another year, the Qin State destroyed the Wei State, and the Qin army was stationed in Lixia. In the forty-two years, Qin State destroyed Chu State. In the second year, he captured Dai Wangjia, killed Yan Wangxi, and destroyed the Yan Kingdom. In the forty-fourth year of King Qi's founding, Qin attacked Qi. The king of Qi followed the prime minister's plan to win later and led his army to surrender to Qin without fighting. Qin captured King Jian of Qi and moved him to Gongcheng. Finally, the state of Qi was destroyed and turned into a county. The world was unified by Qin, and the Qin king established the title of emperor. At first, the king and queen were virtuous, cautious in serving Qin, and had good relations with the princes. Qi was located on the eastern seaboard, and Qin attacked Jin, Yan, and Chu day and night. Facing Qin's attacks, the five countries had to seek self-rescue. Therefore, King Jian of Qi did not suffer from war for more than 40 years in his reign. After the queen died, Hou Sheng became the prime minister of Qi. He accepted a lot of money from Qin spies and sent many guests to Qin. Qin gave them a lot of money. The guests all came back to carry out counterinsurgency activities and persuaded the king of Qi to give up the alliance and return to Qin. Qin was able to destroy the five kingdoms. After the five kingdoms were destroyed, the Qin army finally invaded Linzi, and no one dared to resist. King Jian of Qi surrendered and was moved to Gongcheng.

source: Chen Wan is Chen Ligong's son. When Wan was born, Taishi of Zhou happened to pass by the state of Chen. Chen Ligong asked him to divine divination for Chen Wan. The hexagram obtained was "Guan Gua" changed to "No Gua". Taishi said: The meaning of the hexagram is: observing the customs and sentiments of the country is helpful for being the king's guest. Does this mean that he will obtain the throne of Chen and own the country? Maybe it's not in Chen country but in another country? Or it may not be fulfilled on others, but be fulfilled on his descendants. If it is in another country, it must be the country with the surname Jiang. The surname Jiang is a descendant of the Four Mountains during the reign of Emperor Yao. It is impossible for two things to be powerful at the same time. After the decline of Chen State, his branch will prosper! Li Gong is the youngest son of Chen Wengong, and his mother is a woman from Cai State. After Duke Wen died, Duke Li's brother Chen Bao came to the throne, and this was Duke Huan. Duke Huan and his younger brother Chen were not born from the same mother. When Duke Huan was ill, the people of Cai killed Duke Huan Chen Bao and Prince Chen Min on behalf of Chen Ta, and made Chen Ta the king. This is Duke Li. After Li Gong came to the throne, he married a woman from Cai State. This Cai woman committed adultery with a Cai man and returned to Cai many times. Duke Li also frequently went to Cai. Chen Lin, the youngest son of Duke Huan, resented Duke Li for killing his father and brother, so he asked the people of Cai to trick Duke Li and kill him. Chen Lin established himself as king, this is Duke Zhuang. Therefore, Chen Wan could not be established as the king, but only as the official of the state of Chen. Duke Li was killed because he went abroad for promiscuity, so the Spring and Autumn Annals said that "Cai people killed Chen Ta", which was an accusation against him. After Zhuang Gong died, his younger brother Chujiu came to the throne. This was Chen Xuangong. In the 21st year of Xuangong's reign, Chujiu killed the prince Yu Kou. Yu Kou and Chen Wan were close, and he was afraid that the disaster would involve him, so Chen Wan fled to Qi State. Duke Huan of Qi wanted to appoint him as minister, but he declined and said: "As a humble minister living abroad, I am fortunate enough to be exempted from all kinds of burdens. It is already a favor given to me by you. I dare not hold such a high position again." Duke Huan of Qi appointed him as Gongzheng in charge of hundreds of workers. Qi Yizhong wanted to marry his daughter to Chen Wan, so he conducted a divination for this matter. The result of the divination said: This is called the flying phoenix, with a harmonious sound. The descendants of the Gui family will grow up under the Jiang family. After the Five Dynasties, he will be prosperous and have the same status as Zhengqing. After eight generations, no one can be higher than him. He finally married his daughter to Chen Wan. When Chen Wan fled to Qi, Duke Huan of Qi had been in power for fourteen years. After Chen Wan's death, his posthumous title was Jingzhong. Jingzhong gave birth to Yu Mengyi. After Jingzhong arrived in Qi State, he changed the Chen family name to the Tian family name. Tian Zhen Meng Yi gave birth to Min Meng Zhuang, and Tian Min Meng Zhuang gave birth to Wen Zi Xu Wu. Tian Wenzi served Duke Zhuang of Qi. Luan Cheng, a senior official of the Jin State, caused trouble in the Jin State and fled to the Qi State. Duke Zhuang of Qi gave him generous treatment. Yan Ying and Tian Wenzi advised him, but Duke Zhuang did not listen. Tian Wenzi died, and his son was Huanzi Wuyu.
