Zuo Tiya and I are sisters, and we have the same sons. It would be better to have Tao Mogao carved as a chanyu. Tai Laoya said: Although Mu Moche is young and has ministers to help handle national affairs, if he abandons the noble now and supports the humble, I am afraid there will be trouble in the future. Huhanxie Chanyu finally followed Zhuanquban's suggestion and sculpted Tao Mogao as Chanyu and made a covenant to pass the country to his younger brother in the future. After the death of Hu Hanxie, Diao Tao Mogao came to the throne and was called Fuzhuanruo Qianchanyu.

source: This time when Chanyu came to court, the emperor's additional rewards included 370 sets of clothes, 30,000 pieces of brocade silk, and 30,000 jins of thick silk and cotton. source: Kuang Heng, courtesy name Zhigui, was born in Haicheng County, Cambodia. His grandfather had been farming for generations, and when he came to Kuangheng, he liked to study. Because his family was poor, Kuangheng worked as a hired worker to pay for his expenses. Kuang Heng's energy exceeded ordinary people. Many Confucian scholars praised him and said: Don't talk about "Poetry", Kuang Heng will come; Kuang Heng comes to talk about "Poetry", making people happy and laughing. Kuang Heng was awarded the title of "Jia Ke", but because he failed to pass the "Jia Ke" regulations, he was only appointed as Taichang's storyteller, and later he was appointed as "Pingyuan County Literature". Many scholars wrote letters recommending that Kuang Heng was proficient in classics and was unparalleled in the world. He should be appointed as a literary scholar and go to the capital as an official. The younger generation were willing to follow Kuang Heng to study in Pingyuan County. Kuang Heng should not be an official far away from the capital. The emperor handed this matter over to Prince Taifu Xiao Wangzhi and Shaofu Liang Qiuhe for questioning. Kuang Heng answered with the righteousness of the Book of Songs, which was very profound and brilliant. Xiao Wangzhang reported that Kuang Heng was proficient in classics and his lectures were passed down from a teacher's perspective, which can be viewed. Confucius's son was given the given name Boyu, and his given name was Li; Kong Li's son was given the given name Zisi, and his given name was Ji; Kong Ji's son was given the given name Zishang, and his given name was Bo; Kong Bo's son was given the given name Zijia, and his given name was Qiu; Kong Qiu's son was given the given name Zizhen, and his given name was Ji; Kong Ji's son was given the given name Zigao, and his given name was Chuan. Kong Chuan's son was named Shun, and Kong Shun served as the prime minister of Wei. Kong Shun's son was named Yu. Kong Yu served as Chen She's doctor and died in Chen. Kong Yu's disciple Xiang was Dr. Xiaohui, the Taifu of Changsha. Zixiang's son was named Zhong, and Zhongzhong had two sons: Kong Wu and Kong Anguo. Kong Wu was born in Yannian. Yannian's son was named Ba, named Ciru. Kong Ba's son was Kong Guang. Anguo and Yannian both became doctors during the reign of Emperor Wu by studying "Shangshu". An Guoguan arrived at Linhuai Prefecture. Kong Ba also studied "Shangshu" and followed the Taifu Xiahou Sheng. He was awarded the title of doctor in the last years of Emperor Zhao. During the reign of Emperor Xuan, he served as Taizhong doctor. Because he was selected to teach the classics to the crown prince, he was promoted to Zhanshi and Gaomixiang. At this time, the ministers of the princes and kings were all above the county guards. Emperor Yuan came to the throne, recruited Kong Ba as his teacher, rewarded Kong Ba with the title of Marquis of Guannei, granted him eight hundred households in the city, and gave him the title of Chengjun. Kong Ba is humble and courteous in his treatment of others, and does not like power. He often says that his title is too high and he has no moral character to be qualified for the job! The emperor wanted Kong Ba to serve as prime minister. From the death of Gong Yu, the imperial censor, to the dismissal of Xue Guangde, the emperor always wanted to worship Kong Ba as prime minister. Kong Ba gave way again and again, and the emperor knew that he was sincerely humble, so he did not appoint him as prime minister. After that, the emperor respected Kong Ba even more and his rewards became more generous. After Kong Ba passed away, the emperor came to mourn twice in mourning clothes. He gave Shuyuan's secret utensils, money and silk, and gave them according to the etiquette of the princes, calling him Liejun. Kong Ba had four sons. The eldest son, Mingfu, inherited the title of Marquis of Guannei. The second son Kong Jie and the third son Kong happy both served as school captains and other officials. Kong Guang, the youngest son of Kong Ba, was particularly proficient in Confucian classics. He was elected as Yilang when he was less than twenty years old. Guang Luxun Kuang Heng recommended Kong Guang to be an admonishing doctor because of his good conduct. Because his discussion of political affairs was inconsistent with the emperor's wishes, he was demoted to the magistrate of Hong County. Kong Guang was dismissed in vain and went home to teach Confucian classics. When Emperor Cheng first came to the throne, Liao Guang was elected as a doctor. He was repeatedly asked to be responsible for redressing injustices, regulating customs, and providing relief to victims. Kong Guang successfully completed the mission every time he was ordered to go on an envoy, and Kong Guang's reputation spread throughout the government and the public. At this time, doctors were divided into three subjects to select officials. Those with excellent grades were selected as ministers, and those with lower grades were selected as governors. Those who were not familiar with government affairs were left to serve as princes and tutors in the future. The ones with excellent grades were appointed as ministers, responsible for inspecting the laws, regulations, etiquette and rituals of the previous dynasties. After many years of study, they became proficient in the systems and laws of the Han Dynasty. The emperor trusted him very much and was successively promoted to Pu She and Shan Shu Ling. The emperor had a letter from Shao to commend Kong Guang for his careful and prudent work and never making any mistakes. He was promoted to an official and appointed his son Kong Fang as the minister of ministers to the Huangmen. A few years later, Kong Guang was promoted to the official position Guanglu Dafu, with a salary of 2,000 dan, a reward of 100 jin of gold, and the title of Shangshu. Later, he was promoted to Guang Luxun, still responsible for the affairs of the minister, and served as an official in charge of affairs as before. Kong Guang was in charge of the government affairs for more than ten years, maintaining laws and revising systems. When the emperor asked about political affairs, Kong Guang always answered with the answer he thought was right according to the classic laws, and did not want to be in conflict with the emperor's will. Just as sometimes the emperor did not obey, Kong Guang did not dare to forcefully remonstrate, so Kong Guang served as an official for a long time and was safe. Sometimes he wrote letters to express his opinions, and the memorials he had already written were always deleted and revised. He believed that writing letters to publicize the emperor's faults in order to gain a reputation for loyalty and uprightness was a major sin in officialdom. When Ziguang recommended others to become officials, he was also afraid that others would hear him. When it was my turn to have a holiday, I would go home to rest and talk to my brothers, wives and children about everyday things, but never mention the political affairs surrounding the imperial court.

source: Jingfang, whose courtesy name is Junming, was born in Dunqiu, Shujun County. He studied "The Book of Changes" and studied under Jiao Yanshou from Liang Dynasty. The word for longevity is Gan. Jiao Gan was born in a poor family, but because of his love of learning, he received courtesy from the King of Liang. The King of Liang provided him with the necessary expenses so that he could study with peace of mind. After completing his studies, Jiao Gan served as county historian and was selected to replace Xiaohuang County Magistrate. Because Jiao Gan could often know evil things in advance, the thieves did not dare to commit crimes. Jiao Gan also cared deeply about lower-level officials and ordinary people, so the atmosphere in Xiaohuang County was very good. As a result, his political performance scored very high in the examination, and according to regulations, he should be promoted to another official. However, the three elders of Xiaohuang County wrote a letter expressing their hope to keep Jiao Gan. As a result, the edict was issued to allow Xiaohuang County to keep Jiao Gan and increase his salary. Jiao Gan died in Xiaohuang County. Jiao Gan often said: The person who can get my way but die because of it must be Jingfang. Jiao Gan was the best at talking about disasters. He connected the sixty-four hexagrams with things to be done every day, and used meteorological changes such as wind, rain, cold and temperature as symptoms, each with its own calculation and fulfillment. Jingfang is particularly good at this. Jing Fang is good at the rhythm of bells and knows the rhythm of music. In the fourth year of the Yuan Dynasty, he promoted Xiaolian as a Langguan. During the Yongguang and Jianzhao years, the Xiqiang rebelled, and soon there was a solar eclipse. Then the sky was always dark with no sunlight, and the sky was full of fog with no bright color at all. Jingfang wrote several times, predicting that something was going to happen, whether it was a few months or a year, and what he said came true many times. Emperor Yuan was very happy about this, so he often called Jingfang to ask him. Jingfang replied: In ancient times, emperors selected talents based on merit, so all things were procreated and auspiciousness appeared. But in the declining world, talents were selected only based on praise, so merit was abandoned and disasters appeared. At this time, it is best to let all officials review their own performance, so that the disaster will subside. So Emperor Yuan went to Shao and asked Jingfang to do the work, and Jingfang reported specific methods for inspecting the performance of officials. Emperor Yuan asked the ministers and ministers to go to the Greenhouse Hall with Jingfang to discuss the matter. They all thought that what Jingfang said was too trivial and it was not allowed for superiors and subordinates to supervise each other. The emperor thought so in his heart. At that time, the provincial governors came to the capital to report some matters. Emperor Yuan summoned all the governors and asked the governor to tell them that they wanted to inspect the officials' political performance. The governors also thought it was impossible to implement it. Only the imperial censor Zheng Hong and Guanglu doctor Zhou Kan said no at first, but later thought it was good. At this time, Zhongshu ordered Shi Xian to have exclusive power, and Shi Xian's friend Wulu Chongzong served as Shangshu Ling. He and Jingfang studied the same scripture, but their opinions were very different. When the two were in power, Jingfang was summoned to Emperor Yuan for a banquet, and he asked Emperor Yuan: Why did monarchs like King You and King Li perish? Who did they appoint? The Five Emperors replied: King You and King Li ruled mediocrely, and they only used flattering words to flatter people. Jingfang said: Did King You and King Li appoint these people after knowing that they were clever and sycophants, or did he appoint them because he thought they were virtuous people? Emperor Yuan replied: He appointed them only because he thought they were capable. Jingfang said: So how do you know today that they are not wise men? Emperor Yuan said: It can be known because the society at that time was very chaotic and the monarch failed.

source: In the Wusun Kingdom, Da Kunmi governed Chigu City and was sent to Chang'an for 8,900 miles. There are 120,000 households, a population of 630,000, and an army of 188,800 people. It went as far as Wulei City, the headquarters of the Western Regions Governor, for 1,721 miles, and to the west as far as the hinterland of Kangju and Fan, 5,000 miles. The land is grassy and flat, rainy and the climate is cold. There are many pines on the mountain. The residents do not farm or plant trees, but live with their livestock in search of water and grass, which is the same custom as the Xiongnu. The country is prolific with horses, and wealthy people have as many as four to five thousand horses. The people are strong-willed, greedy for money, unfaithful, and have many thieves. This is a powerful country. He used to submit to the Xiongnu, but later he became powerful and adopted a restrained attitude towards the Xiongnu and refused to go to worship. It borders the Xiongnu in the east, Kangju in the northwest, Dawan in the west, and the Chengguo Kingdoms in the south. Zaojie was originally the land of the Sai people. The Dayue clan defeated and drove away the King of Sai to the west. The King of Sai moved to the south of the county, and the Dayue clan occupied the land of the Sai people. Later, Wusun Kunmo defeated Dayuezhi, and Dayuezhi moved westward and surrendered to Daxia. Wusun Kunmo occupied the original Dayuezhi land, so Wusun residents included Sai people and Dayuezhi people. At first, Zhang Qian said that Wusun and Da Yueshi were originally in Dunhuang. Although Wusun was now stronger, he could still give them some generous gifts to lure them back to their hometown; and then marry the princess to Kunmo, and! The emperor urgently wanted to become a country of brothers and used this method to restrain the Xiongnu. This incident is recorded in "The Biography of Zhang Qian". Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty came to the throne and ordered Zhang Qian to bring gold coins and treasures to Wusun. Kun Mo met Zhang Qian with the attitude of the Xiongnu Chanyu. Zhang Qian was very ashamed and angry, and said to Kun Mo: If you don't thank the emperor for giving you a gift, then return the gift to us. Kunmo stood up and thanked him, but in other respects he remained the same. At the beginning, Kunmo had more than a dozen sons. The middle son Dalu was very strong and good at leading troops. He led more than 10,000 cavalry and lived elsewhere. Dalu's brother was the prince, and the prince had a son named Cen Zuo. The prince died early. Before his death, he said to Kunmo: "Cen Zou must be the prince." Kunmo was sad and agreed. Dalu was very angry about this incident, so he captured all the other brothers, led his soldiers to rebel, and prepared to attack Cen Zuo. Kunmo gave Cen Zuo more than 10,000 cavalry and ordered him to station elsewhere. He also had more than 10,000 cavalry for self-defense. At this time, the country was divided into three parts, all under the control of Kunmo. After Zhang Qian handed over the gifts given to Kunmo by the Han Dynasty, he said to Kunmo: If Wusun can return to his hometown, the Han Dynasty will send the princess as Kunmo's wife. The two countries will become brotherly countries and resist the Xiongnu together. The Xiongnu will definitely be defeated. But Wusun was far away from the Han Dynasty, and the size of the Han Dynasty was unknown. Wusun himself was close to the Xiongnu and had obeyed the Xiongnu for a long time. None of the ministers were willing to move eastward.

source: In the past, the system of the kings, from the emperor, princes to slaves, their official titles, salary, life and death system had different levels. Therefore, different geographical conditions such as land, rivers, lakes, hills, fertile land, plains, and depressions were identified, and the people were taught planting and livestock raising techniques. In this way, the people's supplies for daily life and funerals, including grains, livestock, fish, turtles, birds, beasts, firewood, wood, instruments, and other materials were produced. Production must follow certain seasons, and consumption must be controlled. Before the first month of the lunar calendar, one cannot go into the mountains and forests to cut down trees. Before the first month of the lunar calendar, one cannot go to the rivers and lakes to fish. In addition to complying with seasonal production, they are also not allowed to cut down small trees in the mountains, cut young grass by the lake, catch young insects, fish, or beasts, or collect bird eggs. This is to adapt to the seasonal climate and allow various organisms to reproduce and thrive. In this way, you can give full play to the effects of nature and make all kinds of property reserves abundant. Then, according to the natural conditions of the area, the scholars, farmers, industry and merchants gave full play to their intelligence and physical strength, got up early and went to bed late, managed their own industries, and exchanged with each other: the results of their work met their respective needs. In this way, there is no additional requisition of civilian manpower and material resources, and there is sufficient property in areas near and far. Therefore, the "Book of Changes" says: The monarch uses decrees to determine the changes in nature, assists the heaven and earth to suit the needs of the world, teaches the people to engage in production, produces various kinds of property, uses it in various aspects, and makes various utensils so that the world can benefit. This is the greatness of the sage, and this is what it means. "Guanzi" said: In ancient times, scholars, farmers, workers, and merchants were not allowed to live together. Scholars discuss benevolence and righteousness with each other in the place where they study, craftsmen discuss skills with each other in the government office, businessmen discuss wealth and profit with each other in the market, and farmers discuss farming affairs with each other in the fields. They are engaged in one occupation from morning to night and do not change when things change. Therefore, even if their father and brother's teachings are not strict, they can teach their children well; their children can learn skills even if they do not work hard. They are content with where they live and are happy to pursue their own professions. Even if they see strange and gorgeous items, they will not accept them because they are not suitable for their customs. This is just like the customs of the Rong people and Di people in the northwest and the Wuyue people in the southeast cannot be integrated. In this case, people's desires are few and things are simple, and property is abundant without competition. So the rulers use morality to guide them and use rituals to unify them. Therefore, the common people have integrity and courtesy, value benevolence and righteousness, and despise wealth. This is the summary of why the Xia, Shang and Zhou dynasties were able to develop along the right path and govern the country without resorting to harsh politics. When the Zhou royal family declined and etiquette was destroyed, Duke Zhuang of Lu violated Zhou etiquette by carving on the rafters of his father Huan Gong's temple and dyeing the pillars red.

source: Empress Gao, the Lu family, gave birth to Emperor Hui, who assisted Emperor Gaozu of the Han Dynasty to pacify the world. Her father and brother had three marquises under Emperor Gaozu. After Emperor Hui succeeded to the throne, he honored Empress Lu as the Queen Mother. The Queen Mother made the daughter of Princess Lu Yuan, the sister of Emperor Hui, the Queen. She had no children, so she made the son of a beauty in the harem the Prince. Emperor Hui died, and the prince was established as emperor. The emperor was young, and Empress Dowager Lu came to the court to perform the emperor's affairs and grant amnesty to the world. Later, four of his brother's sons, Lu Tai, Lu Chan, Lu Lu, and Lu Tai's son Lu Tong were made kings, and six Zhu Lu were made princes. The specific details can be found in "Book of Han·Biography of Wai Qi". In the first month of the spring of the first year of Empress Lu's reign, she issued an edict saying: It turned out that Emperor Xiaohui intended to abolish the harsh laws that punished serious crimes and three clans, and regarded wrong words as evil words. He died before the resolution was resolved. It has now been announced that it will be abolished. In February, the people were rewarded with titles of nobility, one level for each household. For the first time, an official with an annual salary of two thousand shi was set up to encourage the world's filial piety. On the fourth day of May in the summer, a fire broke out in the Congtai of Zhao Palace. Liu Qiang, the son of Emperor Xiaohui's harem, was made the King of Huaiyang, Liu Buyi was the King of Hengshan, Liu Hong was the Marquis of Xiangcheng, Liu Chao was the Marquis of Zhi, and Liu Wu was the Marquis of Huguan. In autumn, peaches and plums bloom. In the spring of the second year of Empress Lu's reign, she issued an edict saying: Emperor Gao unified the world and granted fiefs and feudal lordships to all the meritorious officials. All the people were safe and sound, and no one was immune from his kindness. I consider that in the future, due to the passage of time, no one will remember his fame and honor, and will not be able to respect his great righteousness and pass it on to future generations. Now I want to rank the status of each prince in the court according to the size of his merits. I will hide the merit book in the ancestral temple of Emperor Gao and pass it down from generation to generation. His descendants will inherit their merits and titles hereditary. Please work with the princes to submit a proposal. Prime Minister Chen Ping reported: I have discussed with Jianghou Zhoubo, Quzhouhou Lishang, Yinhou Guanying, Anguohou Wang Ling, etc., that the princes were favored and were rewarded with rents and food. Your Majesty also extended extra favors and assigned grades based on merit. Please keep the merit book in the high temple. Empress Lu approved this memorial. On the 27th of the first lunar month of spring, an earthquake occurred and a landslide occurred in Wudu Road. On June 30th in summer, there was a partial solar eclipse. In the seventh month of autumn, Liu Buyi, the king of Hengshan, passed away and eight baht coins were used again. In the summer of the third year of Empress Lu's reign, the Yangtze River and the Han River overflowed, flooding more than 4,000 houses. In autumn, stars appear during the day. In the summer of the fourth year of Empress Lu's reign, the young emperor secretly knew that he was not the empress's biological child, so he complained. The Empress Dowager put him under house arrest in a long alley. The edict said: Anyone who governs the world and governs the people should have a mind that is as inclusive as heaven and as accommodating as the earth. The emperor governs the people from the perspective of caring for the people. Only when the people are sincere and sincere can they respect the emperor. Only when everyone is united can the country be peaceful and the people are safe.
gold_target: Empress Gao, of the Lu family, was the mother of Emperor Hui and assisted Emperor Gaozu in pacifying the realm. After Emperor Hui ascended, she became the Queen Mother. Upon Emperor Hui's death, this prince became emperor, but due to his youth, Empress Dowager Lu ruled in his stead, granting amnesty and promoting her relatives: four of her brother's sons were made kings, and six others were made princes.

source: At this time, Zhu Xuhou Liu Zhang, son of King Qi Hui, was in Kyoto. He was Lu Lu's son-in-law. When he learned of the plot, he immediately sent someone to inform his brother King Qi, asking him to send troops to the west. Liu Zhang prepared to work with Taiwei Zhou Bo and Prime Minister Chen Ping as internal correspondents to kill Zhu Lu. The King of Qi then raised an army, and instigated King Langya and King Liu Ze to mobilize the troops of his country to join forces and march westward. Lu Chan, Lu Lu and others sent General Guan Ying to lead the troops to stop the attack. Guan Ying went to Xingyang, sent people to inform the King of Qi and united with him, waiting for the Lu family to launch a coup before carrying out the execution. Taiwei Zhou Bo conspired with Prime Minister Chen Ping. He believed that Ji, the son of Li Shang, the Marquis of Qu Zhou, was closely related to Lu Lu, so he sent people to force Li Shang to order his son Li Ji to deceive Lu Lu and said: Emperor Gao and Queen Lu jointly established the world. The nine kings established by the Liu family and the three kings established by the Lu family were discussed by the ministers. The discussions and decisions have been informed to all the princes and kings, and all the princes and princes have expressed their approval. Today, the Queen Mother has passed away and the Emperor is young. You are not in a hurry to defend your own kingdoms, but you have gathered troops to stay in Kyoto as generals, which has aroused the suspicion of the ministers and princes. Why not immediately return the general's seal, pass the military power to the Taiwei, ask Liang Wang Lu Chan to return the prime minister's seal, explain it clearly to the ministers, and then return to the feudal country? In this way, the troops can retreat, the ministers can rest assured, and they can sit back and be king of a country thousands of miles away. This is the benefit of all times! Lu Lu agreed to his plan and sent someone to tell Lu Chan and his elders. Some feel uneasy and have different opinions without making a decision. Lu Lu believed in Li Ji and went with him to persuade Zhu Lu. They arrived at the home of Lu Xu's sister, Empress Lu. Lu Xunu said angrily: As a general, you gave up military power, and the Lu family will die without a burial place. She took out all the jewels and jade and threw them in the hall. She said, "I don't have to keep these things for others!" In August, Cao Lan, Marquis of Pingyang, served as the imperial censor and met with Prime Minister Lu Chan to discuss state affairs. The doctor ordered Jia Shou to return Qi, so he accused Lu Chan and said: If you didn't go to your feudal country as soon as possible, can you still leave now if you want to? Tell Lu Chan specifically about Guan Ying's alliance with Qi and Chu. After Pingyang Hou Cao Lan heard about it, he hurriedly informed Prime Minister Chen Ping and Taiwei Zhou Bo. Bo wanted to join the Northern Army, but failed. Marquis Jitong of Xiangping was in charge of Fujie, so he falsely sent military orders in the name of the emperor to let Zhou Bo enter the camp and take charge of the Northern Army. Zhou Bo also sent Li Ji and Dianke Liu Jie to persuade Lu Lu. They said: The emperor sent a Taiwei to take over the Northern Army. If you want everyone to return to the feudal country, you should resign the general and leave, otherwise disaster will be imminent. Lu Lu took off the general's seal and gave it to Liu Jie, and handed over the military power to Taiwei Zhou Bo. Zhou Bo entered the Chinese army's tent and sent an order to the army: Support Lu's right side and Liu's left side. The officers and men were all left-handed. Zhou Bo then took control of the Northern Army. However, there were still Southern troops. Prime Minister Chen Ping summoned Marquis Zhu Xu and Liu Zhang to assist Zhou Bo. Zhou Bo sent Liu Zhang to supervise the military gate and Marquis Pingyang to inform the guards not to let Prime Minister Lu Chan enter the palace gate. Lu Chan did not know that Lu Lu had lost control of the Northern Army and wanted to enter Weiyang Palace to launch a coup. The guards at the palace gate refused to let him in, so he wandered back and forth outside the palace. Pingyang Hou immediately reported to Taiwei Zhou Bo. Zhou Bo was afraid that it would be difficult to win. He did not dare to publicly announce the execution of the Lu family, so he told Zhu Xuhou Liu Zhang: Enter the palace quickly to defend the emperor. Liu Zhang asked Zhou Bo to send thousands of troops to the side gate of Weiyang Palace and saw Lu Chan walking around in the court. At noon, they attacked Lu Chan, but Lu Chan escaped. At this time, strong winds rose sharply, and Lu Chan's entourage was in chaos. No one dared to resist. Liu Zhang led his troops to chase Lu Chan, rushed to the official toilet of Langzhong Mansion and killed him. Liu Zhang had killed Lu Chan, and the Han Emperor sent his attendants to hold the emperor's talisman to comfort Liu Zhang. Liu Zhang wanted to seize the festival, but the attendant refused, so Liu Zhang and his attendants rode in a car together, and rushed into Changle Palace holding the emperor's talisman to kill the Changle Palace guard Lu Gengshi. Liu Zhang returned to the Northern Army and reported the situation to Zhou Bo. Zhou E immediately thanked and congratulated Liu Zhang. He said: The one who fears the most is Lu Chan. Now that Lu Chan has been executed, the world will be at peace. So he beheaded Lu Lu and flogged Lu Xunu. They sent out men and horses to capture the men and women of Lu, and killed them all regardless of old or young. The ministers conspired with each other. They thought that the young emperor and his three younger brothers who were kings were not the sons of Emperor Hui, so they killed them all and enthroned Emperor Wen. The story is recorded in the "Book of Han·Zhou Bo and Gao Wu Wang Biography". Ban Gu commented: When Emperor Hui of the Han Dynasty was Xiao Hui and Empress Gao, the world was freed from the pain of war, and the monarchs and ministers wanted to rule by doing nothing. Therefore, Emperor Hui bowed down to bring peace to the world, and Empress Gao used women to preside over government affairs. The world was peaceful without leaving the palace, punishments were used sparingly, and the people could only work on farming, so that they had enough food and clothing.
